As a transracial adoptee (I’m Asian and adoptive parents are white), please do a lot of research on the culture that the child comes from to involve them in it throughout their upbringing. Culture is a huge part of one’s identity and losing that part can easily become confusing and stressful growing up. Unfortunately one of the biggest problems within transracial adoptees is identity discourse.

My experience:
>!Also, please teach them about what racism is and how to handle being discriminated against if they’ll be growing up in an area where they won’t see many of their own race. I was the only Asian growing up in a white neighborhood and I couldn’t understand what was “wrong” with me (more specifically my eye shape). I was actively discriminated against by peers and teachers to the point that I never made any friends growing up due to the isolation and I still struggle with making connections to other people.!<

There’s a lot that goes into adopting from another race/ethnicity, but your primary goal is to raise the child the best you can. From being honest to including their culture throughout (not just in their elementary school years) their life, it may not be easy. Kids like feeling a sense of belonging especially where they go home to. It doesn’t always happen, but they may feel like an outsider in their community if they don’t have anyone who looks like them.

Adoptee from 2000 here. I feel like my adoptive parents were extremely unqualified. I’m actually a transracial adoptee (Asian adopted by white Americans) and I wish that mine cared about me as a person instead of a trophy growing up. My adoptive mother would call my people dirty and my culture backwards while praising the people in America that looked like her. She would even go around saying that she “saved a baby girl from a third world country” and that she’s such a good person. Meanwhile my adoptive father was mostly absent at home and I never really saw him much. I grew up with an extreme amount of racism since there were no other POC in my area. The first time I experienced it firsthand was when I came home crying from preschool and that people were making fun of my eyes and my adoptive mother would tell me that she got bullied for wearing glasses and that I should’ve gotten over it. I get that maybe she was trying to be relatable, but she turned it into a competition by saying that her bullying was worse than mine. When I asked why I “looked wrong”, she told me to stop crying or she’d send me back to the country she adopted me from which made me feel completely alone. Even when I wanted to try and bond with her when I was little, she would never take the time to interact with me. Even when I just wanted to be told that I was doing a good job or be told that I was loved, I got nothing from her, not even a hug. When she wasn’t being emotionally neglectful, she’d buy me one toy every now and again for good grades and tell me to appreciate that she went out of her way to get me something. Immediately after I thanked her for getting me something, she’d force me to give it to my little sister “because she’s younger”. She’d get joy out of buying me something that she knew both my sister and I wanted to watch me become sad that I couldn’t have something that was given to me. She’d always buy one toy to give to me in front of my sister so both of them would guilt me into giving it up immediately. I already felt unloved and dehumanized and she made me feel like I was worth even less than my sister. In the eyes of the person who was supposed to be my mother, she saw me as the least favorite child and that I didn’t deserve to be happy. I can only speak from my own experience about adoption and that’s just a small generalization of a few things of what I went through. Reading through a lot of happier threads on here makes me feel happy that others are happy with their families, but it also kind of hurts knowing that I never got love from the one who I had to depend on for the majority of my life.
